tasks.short: Liaise with physicist and supportive care colleagues

steps.what: Act as liaison with physicist and supportive care personnel about patient needs and concerns

tasks.design: Retain liaison as direct communication between responsible professionals. No message drafting task is added to create an artificial automation baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: The value is clarification and coordination around a particular patient's situation.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported means of removing the professional conversation is established.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising which concern needs immediate clarification and obtaining a shared understanding.
tasks.human_edge: Notice uncertainty and challenge an unsafe assumption.
tasks.altitude: Improve the quality of clinical handovers and shared responsibilities.

reach.learn: Clarify the treatment context without exceeding professional responsibility

evidence.claim: Clinical liaison remains a professional conversation; no task specific labour gain is established.

assumptions: The therapist obtains and verifies the context during s1; colleagues provide answers during the conversation rather than as a free structured handover.
No treatment change is autonomously initiated.
The workflow is unchanged, so additional system upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Frequency and urgency of liaison contacts
research_questions: Which misunderstandings lead to repeated handovers?

incremental.description: No additional software or operating process

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100: liaison remains fully human, yielding zero gross and net savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Capture patients' availability and verify scheduling constraints against approved treatment instructions
Match treatment times to verified duration, resource and availability constraints
Review treatment times, resolve conflicts and confirm appointments with patients

tasks.design: Configure appointment matching in the existing treatment scheduling category represented by {OPS_SYSTEM}, with {CALENDAR} resource availability. The therapist captures and checks constraints before matching and approves each final appointment proposal before booking and patient confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Staff repeatedly compared patient availability with equipment and staffing calendars.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scheduling rules can propose slots from explicit constraints without inferring a clinical priority.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving conflicts without changing prescribed treatment requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Explain difficult choices and escalate clinical constraints to the responsible practitioner.
tasks.altitude: Manage scheduling exceptions rather than manually compare every slot.

reach.learn: Separate availability preferences from clinical requirements

evidence.claim: Native scheduling can match supplied duration, resource and availability constraints; the proposed radiation scheduling savings are model knowledge, not a measured case.

assumptions: Before s1 the responsible treatment team produces approved treatment instructions through its unchanged clinical planning process; its time and approvals are not claimed as savings here.

In s1 the therapist verifies and captures patient identity, allowable dates and intervals, duration, required equipment, staffing requirements and patient availability. All transcription, clarification and missing constraint resolution are counted in 35 hours.
Resource owners maintain equipment and staff availability calendars through their existing process; added reconciliation support is charged below. Stale calendars stop automatic proposals.
The matcher never produces a readiness, urgency or treatment suitability flag. Missing instructions or unsatisfied constraints return to manual scheduling in s3.
Native scheduling is evaluated before building an integration; the proposal changes no prescribed regimen.
unknowns: Existing scheduling features and quality of resource calendars
Proportion of appointment conflicts requiring clinical review
research_questions: Does native slot matching reduce total scheduling time after constraint capture and patient confirmation?

already_counted.description: Constraint capture, review, conflict resolution and patient confirmation

incremental.description: Scheduling rule upkeep and reconciliation of booked slots

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, dates, times, resources and verified treatment constraints; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 task scenarios: B=100 and R=65 yield 35 gross and 27 net after 8 focal upkeep hours. Range 0-7 allows existing scheduling automation and substantial conflict work; no clinical planning saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Train and supervise radiotherapy technologists through demonstration, observation, feedback and intervention

tasks.design: Keep practical teaching and supervision with a qualified therapist. Digital teaching materials do not replace observation or intervention during care.
tasks.previous_blocker: A learner's safe practice must be observed in context.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes the hands on supervision named in this task.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising a learner's misunderstanding before it affects care.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt instruction and intervene at the right moment.
tasks.altitude: Strengthen the quality of feedback and safe progression.

reach.learn: Use observation based feedback and clear intervention thresholds

evidence.claim: The digest describes documentation assistance rather than replacement of practical radiotherapy supervision; no task labour saving is established.

assumptions: The supervisor produces the performance assessment through direct observation in s1; no competence flag or automated sign off is assumed.
Creating course materials or training records is not invented as a baseline for this supervision task.
No new deployment means no additional upkeep.
research_questions: What feedback most reliably prevents repeated practical errors?

incremental.description: No added system or monitoring work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100: practical teaching and supervision remain fully human; zero gross and net savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use checked scheduling constraints to reduce slot comparisons while protecting direct care coordination and supervision.
reach: Help patient representatives distinguish access needs from clinical scheduling constraints
role.ambitious_version: A therapist with less manual appointment matching and preserved time for patients, colleagues and learners.
